candidates.summary: Round-1 'block parser swallows lines' still reproduces: an unclosed $$ (or \\[) line opens a display block whenever the delimiter appears on any later line within 8KB, across blank lines, headings, code fences and container ends
candidates.failure_scenario:
A page (or a board realm rendering user posts) with one unclosed '$$' line followed within 8KB by any later '$$', e.g. '$$
oops forgot to close

## Section 2

More text with $$y$$ here.': hasClosingLine finds the inline '$$y$$' two blocks down, the block opens, and the heading and paragraph render as one run of italic math letters ('## Section 2' becomes <merror>?#</merror><mi>S</mi>...), leaving 'y$$ here.' as text. When the later '$$' sits inside a fenced code block, the math swallows the fence opener and the fence's closing ``` opens a new fence that never closes, so everything to the end of the page renders as code. A '$$' inside a blockquote or list item is closed by a '$$' outside its container and takes the quoted/listed text with it. The author's thread reply says the block 'only opens on $$ / \[ when a closing delimiter actually follows'; the delimiter found can belong to a different block, and TestMathDoesNotSwallowText only pins the shape with no later delimiter.
